match.reason: The bank point is about epidemiology as the study of population health patterns, not the community-based, needs-driven, skills-building and sustainability principles that make aid programs work, so it does not teach the same idea.

draft.title: What makes a program work
card: A health program works best when it is run with the community, not just for it. Local people help plan it, make decisions and take part in it.
It targets real needs. The program tackles a problem that the community has identified and that evidence shows is affecting its health.
It builds local skills. Training local people, such as health workers, means the knowledge stays in the community after outside staff leave.
It can be sustained. The program can carry on over time with local people, local resources and steady funding, without relying on outside help forever.
draft.remember: A program works best when the community shares in it, its aim matches a real need, and local skills keep it going.

a.q: Which feature of a health program best shows that it builds local skills?
opts: Village volunteers are trained to run the clinic themselves
Overseas doctors treat patients at the clinic each month
The clinic is built using donated money from abroad
The clinic is opened by a visiting government minister
a.why: Training local people leaves knowledge in the community after outside staff go. Overseas doctors treating patients may help for a time, but the skills leave with them, so that does not build local skills.
a.clue: Which option leaves new abilities with local people?

b.q: An organisation builds a clinic in a remote town in Laos, but never asks residents what they need. Most families are more concerned about unsafe drinking water, and the clinic is rarely used. Which feature of a working program is most clearly missing?
opts: Targeting a real need identified by the community
Building local skills through training health workers
Sustaining the program with steady funding over time
Running the program with a large number of staff
b.why: Residents were not asked, so the program did not target the need they faced, which was unsafe water. Training and funding may matter too, but the scenario does not say they are the problem. Staff numbers are not a feature of a working program.
b.clue: Think about what the families said mattered most to them.

a.best: Village volunteers are trained to run the clinic themselves

b.best: Targeting a real need identified by the community

problems.detail: The card gives four features, with sustainability as its own feature that relies on local people, local resources and steady funding. The remember line folds sustainability into 'local skills keep it going', which drops it as a separate feature and suggests skills alone keep a program going.
The clue says 'what the families said mattered most to them', but the scenario says residents were never asked. This contradicts the scenario and could confuse students.
